output.summary: A perennial deciduous woody vine native to forests of northern China, the Russian Far East, Korea and Japan, it produces smooth red berries in dense hanging clusters. Its crushed leaves smell lemony and can be eaten as a vegetable, while Koreans make the berries into a cordial drink called omija-cha.
